original_value: Multi-person pose estimation aims to detect human keypoints from images with multiple persons. Bottom-up methods for multi-person pose estimation have attracted extensive attention, owing to the good balance between efficiency and accuracy. Recent bottom-up methods usually follow the principle of keypoints localization and grouping, where relations between keypoints are the keys to group keypoints. These relations spontaneously construct a graph of keypoints, where the edges represent the relations between two nodes (i.e., keypoints). Existing bottom-up methods mainly define relations by empirically picking out edges from this graph, while omitting edges that may contain useful semantic relations. In this paper, we propose a novel Dynamic Graph Convolutional Module (DGCM) to model rich relations in the keypoints graph. Specifically, we take into account all relations (all edges of the graph) and construct dynamic graphs to tolerate large variations of human pose. The DGCM is quite lightweight, which allows it to be stacked like a pyramid architecture and learn structural relations from multi-level features. Our network with single DGCM based on ResNet-50 achieves relative gains of 3.2% and 4.8% over state-of-the-art bottom-up methods on COCO keypoints and MPII dataset, respectively.

result.paraphrase: Multi-person pose estimation seeks to identify human keypoints in images containing several people. Bottom-up approaches have drawn considerable interest because they strike a strong balance between efficiency and accuracy. Recent bottom-up methods generally adopt a keypoint localization-and-grouping strategy, in which relationships among keypoints are crucial for assembling them. These relationships naturally form a keypoint graph, whose edges denote the links between two nodes, that is, keypoints. Most existing bottom-up methods define these relations by manually selecting edges from the graph, thereby ignoring edges that may encode meaningful semantic connections. In this paper, we introduce a new Dynamic Graph Convolutional Module (DGCM) to capture rich relations in the keypoint graph. In particular, we consider all relations, namely all graph edges, and build dynamic graphs to better handle large variations in human poses. DGCM is highly lightweight, enabling pyramid-style stacking and the learning of structural relations from multi-level features. Our ResNet-50 network with a single DGCM achieves relative improvements of 3.2% and 4.8% over state-of-the-art bottom-up methods on the COCO keypoints and MPII datasets, respectively.
